rounds.proof_sketch: For input shape [16, 256, 256] with dim=1 reduction: dim1=256, blockDim.x=256, so elements_per_thread = (256 + 256 - 1) / 256 = 511 / 256 = 1 (integer division). Original: start_idx = tid * 1 = tid. Mutated: start_idx = tid / 1 = tid. Both expressions evaluate identically when elements_per_thread = 1.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes `tid * elements_per_thread` to `tid / elements_per_thread` on line 41 of the dim1 reduction kernel. However, for the fixed input shape [16, 256, 256], when reducing over dimension 1, dim1=256 and blockDim.x=256. This gives elements_per_thread = (256 + 255) / 256 = 1. When elements_per_thread equals 1, both multiplication (tid * 1 = tid) and division (tid / 1 = tid) produce identical results. Therefore, every thread computes the same start_idx in both original and mutated versions, making the mutation semantically equivalent under this fixed-shape contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation would only be distinguishable if dim1 > 256 (causing elements_per_thread > 1), but the shape [16, 256, 256] is fixed. No value-level changes can make elements_per_thread != 1.
rounds.recommendations: When designing mutation testing for CUDA kernels with dynamic work distribution, ensure test configurations exercise multiple values of derived quantities like elements_per_thread. A shape like [16, 512, 256] would make elements_per_thread=2 and expose this mutation. Consider parameterized shape testing when shape-dependent behavior is suspected.
